title: The Review tab leads with what needs the developer and where to look
context: At G1 the developer confirms the summary in the conversation and does not reread the Proposal (ADR-0060), so the developer's reading cost sits almost entirely at G2. On the triage-state-mapping Review, the one question the developer had to answer sat in the fifth section, after tables of results, verification, findings and a diff.
decision: The Review tab runs, in order: what the developer must decide or do, where to focus the review, deviations from the Proposal, acceptance results by scenario, the test plan, and after-release steps when there are any; verification detail, code review findings and residual risks follow collapsed. What needs the developer comes first because G2 is where the developer's reading cost sits.

alternatives.option: Keep a boundary-relevant diff on every Review
alternatives.reason: It is an excerpt of what the pull request shows in full, and it cost more to render than it told the reader.

alternatives.option: List developer-run tests only in the section that asks the developer to act
alternatives.reason: The test plan is the one place every check lives; that section points at the developer-run items instead.

consequences: The Review carries no code diff by default, because the pull request carries the full diff; a deviation may carry a short one.
Each test plan item names its executor, agent or developer, and an agent-run item reports its result in place.
A Review with nothing to decide and no deviations can be accepted after reading its first sections.
Scenario results and test plan items are data rendered as cards, so a missing result is caught mechanically.
